name: STAR Attitude — TRIAD and Davenport's q-method
summary: Attitude from vector observations: TRIAD for two directions and Davenport's q-method (Wahba's problem) for 2 to 1000 weighted directions, with the eigenproblem solved by Jacobi rotations in the standard library; conversion to the attitude matrix and the Wahba loss; within 7e-15 of SciPy's SVD solution and 5e-16 of ahrs TRIAD on 401 attitudes.
reference: By hand (no published numerical example cited): a body frame turned by +90 degrees about z has the attitude matrix ((0, 1, 0), (-1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1)) and the quaternion (cos 45, 0, 0, sin 45); method of Wahba (1965), Black (1964), Davenport (1968)

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: b = A r, reference to body; quaternion (w, x, y, z) scalar first with w >= 0; matrices as tuples of rows
review.G-06: no external data; cross-check corpus generated with a fixed seed
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO, no state
review.G-13: ValueError for every invalid input and for observations that do not fix an attitude; sensitivity of nearly parallel observations stated in the README
